name: Question 13
problem: Which of the following gives the total area enclosed by graph of the polar curve $r=2\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \pi ?$
worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\text{d}\theta \,.
$$

When $r(\theta )=2\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )$, ${\theta }_{1}=0$ and ${\theta }_{2}=\pi $, this gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta ))^{2}\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

Which of the following gives the total area enclosed by graph of the polar curve r=2θ+cos⁡(θ) for 0≤θ≤π?

a
2∫02π(θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ
b
12∫0π(2θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ
c
12∫0π/2(θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ
d
12∫02π(θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ
e
2∫0π(θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The area bounded by a polar curve is given by A=12∫θ1θ2r2(θ)dθ.

When r(θ)=2θ+cos⁡(θ), θ1=0 and θ2=π, this gives

A=12∫0π(2θ+cos⁡(θ))2dθ.
